summary: Three-story Art Deco lookout in Yellowstone, mostly reinforced concrete with a steel observation tower, built 1939-41 to replace a 1921 stone lookout; the NPS staffs it each summer and it is a popular day-hike destination.

facts.design: Three-story Art Deco lookout of mostly reinforced concrete with a steel observation tower, about 25 ft square; first floor public restrooms, second floor spotter's residence and storage, third floor observation level; replaced a 1921 stone lookout

staffing.status: continuously staffed from mid-June until the fire season ends (NPS)

access.note: Day-hike destination in Yellowstone National Park; interpretive exhibits are inside the base of the lookout (NPS). The lookout is also a working fire station.

visit.trail_note: Hiking trails start at the Dunraven Pass trailhead and at the Chittenden Road parking area (NPS); HABS notes a tower access road (Chittenden Road) and a parking area north of the building.

facts.agency: National Park Service, Yellowstone National Park

events.note: Stone masonry shelter and fire lookout built on the summit with a $2,500 appropriation; replaced later
Three-mile telephone line built from Dunraven Pass to the fire-lookout station
John D. Coffman observed that the 1921 lookout was inadequate and called for significant renovation
Theodore Robb served as ranger naturalist and fire lookout at the top
Park Service decided to raze the existing structure and build anew; construction began June 1939
New three-story reinforced concrete lookout completed (HABS and the NHLR Built field); the NHLR narrative says completed in summer 1940
Two-story precast concrete addition for telecommunications equipment, with an interpretive center on the second floor

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR narrative says construction began in June 1939 and was completed the following summer, 1940; the NHLR Built field and HABS say 1941. The record keeps 1941 and the story reports both.
NHLR and firelookout.com give 10,243 ft (3,122 m) for the lookout site; the NPS gives 10,219 ft (3,115 m) as the peak elevation. The record's 3122.1 m matches NHLR; no change proposed.
NHLR gives outer dimensions of 25 ft 5 in by 24 ft 5 in; HABS describes a 25 ft 6 in square building. The story gives no dimensions.

notes_for_editor: Build date is contested: the NHLR Built field and HABS say 1941, but the NHLR narrative says construction began June 1939 and was completed summer 1940. The record keeps 1941; the story reports both. The 1921 stone lookout (Willhite, HABS, NHLR) is treated as the predecessor. The NPS page is undated; its staffing statement is in the present tense. Drive-up status rests on HABS (a parking area north of the building; the lookout described as the only Yellowstone fire lookout facility accessible by vehicle) plus two NPS hiking trails. Road seasonality and whether the upper floors are open to visitors were not checked. No fire events beyond the staffing history and the 1980 modification appear in the sources read. No climbing advice is given.
